body:
### Describe the bug

On our network (corporate, some TLS/traffic inspection in the path), gh 2.100.0 fails every HTTPS request with an instant connection reset — auth, api calls, everything. gh 2.89.0 works fine, same machine, same network, tested side by side in the same minute to rule out the network just being flaky.

Not GitHub-specific — 2.100.0 fails the same way against other hosts (e.g. `example.com`). curl sending the identical request succeeds. So something changed in the client between these versions that this network's middlebox doesn't like — not a GitHub API issue, and probably not a universal break for everyone on 2.100.0, since a lot more people would be reporting this if it were.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.100.0 (2026-09-03)
```

Works fine on 2.89.0. Confirmed by running both binaries back-to-back on the same machine/network/minute — 2.100.0 fails 3/3, 2.89.0 succeeds 3/3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --scopes repo`
2. Approve the browser prompt
3. See error

Same thing on token-based login and plain `gh api` calls.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: login/API calls work like they do on 2.89.0.

Actual: instant connection reset, ~50ms in, on every request.

### Logs

```
$ gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --scopes repo
failed to authenticate via web browser: Post "https://github.com/login/device/code": read tcp 10.23.41.14:55833->140.82.113.4:443: read: connection reset by peer
```

```
$ gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --scopes repo
error validating token: Get "https://api.github.com/": read tcp 10.23.41.14:56184->140.82.113.6:443: read: connection reset by peer
```

```
$ GH_TOKEN=<redacted> gh api --hostname example.com /
Get "https://example.com/api/v3/": read tcp 10.23.41.14:56609->104.20.23.154:443: read: connection reset by peer
```

curl with the same headers/token/UA against the same host works fine:

```
$ curl -H "Authorization: token <redacted>" https://api.github.com/
401
```

macOS, arm64, corporate network with some traffic inspection appliance in the path. Happy to grab `GH_DEBUG=api` output or a packet capture if useful — flagging that this may be specific to whatever's inspecting traffic on our network rather than a universal 2.100.0 break, since I couldn't find other reports pinned to this exact version.

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed report and for narrowing this down by testing 2.89.0 vs 2.100.0 side by side. I could not confirm a specific change in `cli/cli` (the HTTP transport setup in `api/client.go` looks unchanged) or in the `cli/go-gh` client library between those versions that would explain an immediate TCP reset, so I cannot yet point to a concrete root cause. Since 2.100.0 also fails against a non-GitHub host with identical behavior via curl succeeding, this looks environment-specific (likely the corporate inspection appliance reacting to something distinguishing about this Go build, such as its TLS ClientHello fingerprint, rather than a `gh`-specific bug), but I cannot verify that without more data. Suggesting `bug` and `investigation-needed` since this needs a repeatable diagnosis before engineering can act, plus `gh-auth` since the reproduction is centered on `gh auth login`/token validation. It would help to get `GH_DEBUG=api` output or a packet capture from a failing request, and ideally to bisect a few releases between 2.89.0 and 2.100.0 to narrow down which one introduced the regression. No duplicate reports of this exact symptom were found in `cli/cli`.

Thanks for reporting this, @gloox! 🙏 

Can you please share the log output of these commands with us? (redact where needed)

```shell
GH_DEBUG=api gh auth login
GH_DEBUG=api gh release download --repo cli/cli
gh config list
```

(The 2nd one is an unauthenticated command)

We had some bug changes in our HTTP client in `v2.100.0`, but they're just about custom API hosts and trust. What I see in your case is in a lower level. A gut feeling says maybe it's related to Go HTTP client details, but I'm not really confudent to blame Go stdlib (latest `gh` is built with go1.26.8  toolchain). To rule that out I'd recommend you to build `gh` with the latest go1.27 to see if anything changes.

Heres the additional info:

```
failed to authenticate via web browser: Post "https://github.com/login/device/code": read tcp 10.23.41.14:62204->140.82.113.4:443: read: connection reset by peer
```

**`gh config list`:**

 My gh 2.100 is built with go1.27.1 and 2.89 is using go1.26.1

Can you try with ~~the first one of these~~ `GODEBUG` values set in your env:

```shell
GODEBUG=http2client=0  gh release download --repo cli/cli
```

(Taken from official docs at https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#hdr-HTTP_2)
Do you also have this problem on `v2.99.0` or `v2.90.0`?

I think this is almost certainly https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81199. Homebrew builds the `gh` formula with go1.27.1, and I suspect since you are on Mac, you probably got your installation from homebrew.

The TL;DR seems to be that your network appliance is not behaving correctly with spec-compliant changes in Go. Perhaps if you can weigh in on that issue providing more details about your appliance vendor and software, the Go team might consider changes here.

In the meantime it seems like your best workarounds are:
 * To downgrade to an older version
 * To use v2.100.0 from our release artifacts (but we are likely to bump to 1.27 for the next release anyway)

@babakks Both v2.90.0 and v2.99.0 work fine. There's no reset, normal responses and only v2.100.0 fails.

I downloaded each release binary directly and ran it against the same repro:

```
curl -sL -o gh290.zip https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v2.90.0/gh_2.90.0_macOS_arm64.zip
unzip gh290.zip -d gh290
GH_TOKEN=<token> ./gh290/gh_2.90.0_macOS_arm64/bin/gh release download --repo cli/cli -p "*.txt"
# works

curl -sL -o gh299.zip https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v2.99.0/gh_2.99.0_macOS_arm64.zip
unzip gh299.zip -d gh299
./gh299/gh_2.99.0_macOS_arm64/bin/gh release download --repo cli/cli -p "*.txt"
# works

gh release download --repo cli/cli -p "*.txt"
# same error as before (connection reset)
```

`GODEBUG=http2client=0` also fixes it on v2.100.0:

```
GODEBUG=http2client=0 gh release download --repo cli/cli -p "*.txt"
# works
```

@williammartin thanks, downgrading to v2.89.0 is what I've been running since.

I saw this both in the office (on the corporate network directly) and now at home over VPN, so it's not tied to being tunneled.

> I downloaded each release binary directly and ran it against the same repro.

Can you do the same with v2.100.0 (try the release binary directly)?

If it does reproduce, can you also give me the output of:

```
gh version <path to downloaded2.00.0>
```

title: gh 2.100.0 fails HTTPS requests with an instant connection reset
